notes:
High-level summary: Clinify builds a HIPAA-sensitive search layer for multi-hospital systems (EMR connectors + FHIR ingestion). Primary ask: highly accurate embeddings + reranking stack to prioritize exact clinical findings and codes (ICD/CPT) while keeping PHI fully contained.

Scale + perf requirements: plan to index 30M-120M clinical notes (avg ~1.2k tokens/note). Expected peak QPS 400-800 for triage+search, tail latency targets: 95th percentile <150ms for embedding-lookup+ANN, <300ms end-to-end for reranking flows. Cost sensitivity: target cost-per-query <$0.002 (strict for enterprise budget).

Security & ops constraints: "We cannot transmit PHI off-prem" - CTO; must support private control plane or on-prem runtime, full BAA, immutable audit logs (90+ day retention), per-user access controls, SSO/SAML, KMS with HSM-backed keys, and data residency in NA. They insist on network diagram and port-level firewall rules before any on-prem install.

POC notes: SE Maya ran POC using local Milvus cluster + Redwood runtime overlay; observations: good quality on rerank (MRR up ~14%) but batching and kernel selection need tuning for shorter clinical queries. Found an edge case with long discharge summaries where KV cache miss rate increases latency.

Sales touches: AE (Ethan) has been nudging security for BAA; finance asked for a line-itemed pricing deck (linked). Procurement wants a direct comparison vs Elastic + Pinecone on TCO for 5-year committed capacity.

Decision criteria quoted from CIO: "Must be audit-first, deterministic latency under heavy load, and predictable unit economics — we cannot have surprise egress or per-token spikes."
